title: Send Your Name to Saturn's Largest Moon
summary:
NASA is getting ready to send a robot helicopter to a faraway moon — and your name can ride along. The spacecraft is called Dragonfly, an eight-bladed rotorcraft headed for Titan, the largest of Saturn's 292 known moons. Its launch is planned for no earlier than July 2028, and after more than six years of travel, it would reach Titan in 2034.

As part of its Journey to Titan campaign, NASA has opened an online registry for names to be placed on a microchip aboard the spacecraft. Signers will get a digital boarding pass. The names will not help run the mission, but Nicky Fox, NASA's Science Mission Directorate associate administrator, said the agency is excited to bring humanity along and invites everyone to join the small but mighty rotorcraft's journey.

Titan is a longtime dream destination in the search for life beyond Earth. It has dusty dunes overlooking lakes and rivers of methane, and a surface near minus 290 degrees Fahrenheit, inhospitable to life as we know it. Yet a giant ocean hides beneath its icy shell. Astrobiologists widely agree those waters probably contain enough complex compounds to support a prebiotic environment, and laboratory simulations have indicated Titan's atmosphere can form some building blocks for DNA and RNA. If true, microbial life may exist in the moon's hidden waters — but no one can confirm it without going there.

That is Dragonfly's job. After landing, it will hop to different places during a planned three-year mission, traveling 70 miles and visiting 20 to 30 areas while searching for signs of habitability. Dragonfly is under construction at the Johns Hopkins Applied Physics Laboratory in Laurel, Maryland, as the fourth mission in NASA's New Frontiers Program. Sign-ups close at 11:59 p.m. EST on January 15, 2027.
why_it_matters: Exploring Titan's hidden ocean could help answer whether life can exist beyond Earth, and the name registry lets the public share in a mission that tests that big question firsthand.

background_read: Titan is a large moon that orbits the planet Saturn, and it is covered by a thick atmosphere that hides its surface from view.

Scientists are interested in Titan because it has lakes and rivers of liquid methane and a hidden ocean of water beneath its icy outer shell, which could hold the ingredients needed for life to begin.
Dragonfly is a rotorcraft built to fly through Titan's thick air and hop from place to place, sampling the ground and air to look for signs that the moon could support life.
Sending a flying explorer lets scientists study many different areas of Titan instead of staying in one spot, which is why the mission was planned as a long journey to a distant world.
